source.title: [Paper] All's Fair In Love And Love: Copy Suppression in GPT-2 Small

record.file_problem: The full blog post is present; the linked paper itself is not included.
record.tranche_reason: It reports experiments on copy suppression's contribution to self-repair in the IOI task, bearing on the backup/self-repair claim, but does not reproduce the original circuit analysis.
record.gate_note: The post also reports copy-suppression results on general text, anti-induction scores, and semantic similarity. Those results do not test the IOI circuit versions. Its 76.9% figure concerns explaining L10H7's copy-suppression behavior, not IOI circuit faithfulness.
record.test_reason: It runs ablation experiments on GPT-2 small in the IOI task to explain how self-repair works (V2). The headline self-repair result attributes part of the negative-head self-repair to copy suppression. It also shows that an IOI circuit component, negative name mover L10H7, runs a general algorithm across OpenWebText, which bears on V3's component-reuse part. All IOI results in the post are qualitative; numbers are deferred to the linked paper.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors add that self-repair in IOI takes qualitatively different forms. They also say copy suppression resolves the negative-head self-repair noted in the original IOI paper, yet explains only part of IOI self-repair. They state they are left with open questions.
record.recipe_differences: The post describes copy-suppression-focused experiments and ablation, not the original IOI circuit identification and faithfulness, completeness, and minimality evaluation.

fits_no_version.finding: Copy suppression heads treat semantically similar tokens (capitalisation, plurals, tense) as the same token, beyond what embedding cosine similarity predicts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Copy-suppression heads use a semantic token-similarity notion not captured by embedding cosine similarity.

record.problems: The IOI self-repair results are qualitative in this post; it does not provide numerical outcomes, uncertainty, or sufficient intervention and head-level details to assess the specific backup-head role.
record.rows_left_out: The reported L10H7 copy-suppression metrics, anti-induction correlation, and semantic-similarity findings concern copy suppression beyond the IOI backup-head claim and were not included as rows.

untested.parts: The 26-head, 7-class circuit and its faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria.
Which specific backup name-mover heads take over, and how much logit difference is restored; no numbers are in the post.
IOI circuits in other models, sizes and training checkpoints. The post mentions larger models only for copy suppression, not for IOI.
Sensitivity of IOI circuit evaluation to ablation, metric or prompt distribution. The KL caveat concerns the L10H7 analysis only.

missing.what: L10H7 (an IOI negative name mover) performs copy suppression across OpenWebText; CSPA recovers 76.9% of its behaviour. This is component reuse beyond IOI.
missing.locator: Key Results: Copy Suppression; Copy Suppression-Preserving Ablation

missing.what: Strong correlation between heads' anti-induction scores and their IOI indirect-object suppression scores, in the quadrant where both are positive.
Weight-based (Q-composition) relationships between name-mover heads and self-repair heads, changing attention to names.
Unembedding directions do not explain self-repair well (paper Section 4.2, cited).

record.verdict_notes: This is a blog post summarising arXiv:2310.04625; the quantitative IOI self-repair results are in the paper, not here. The 76.9% figure concerns L10H7's general behaviour, not IOI circuit faithfulness. The reader's V3 'not_tested' overlooks the component-reuse part.

versions.untested_parts: The 26-head, 7-class circuit and its faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria.
The post does not specify that the main name-mover heads were ablated, identify the backup heads, or detail which roles they assume.
Other models, sizes, training checkpoints, and component reuse across tasks.
Comparison of circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or metrics for recovering the IOI circuit.
Sensitivity of the IOI circuit evaluation to ablation, metric, or prompt distribution.
IOI performance across name orders, templates, and prompts with more names.

rows.subject: GPT2-Small
rows.operation_detail: Ablate copying in IOI experiments; the post does not specify the exact component or ablation details.

conditions.value: copying ablated; exact details not stated

rows.measure: Self-repair and the contribution of copy suppression to it
rows.value: Copy suppression explains some, but not all, of the self-repair; the post describes ablation of copying as leaving nothing to copy-suppress.
rows.note: Qualitative report; the post does not give numerical results or identify the specific heads involved.
rows.check: The measure is how much of self-repair is attributable to copy suppression, not whether self-repair occurs. Self-repair itself is reported as present. 'Explains some, but not all' is a statement about mechanism, not a weaker V2 effect, so state is observed for self-repair occurring. Baseline and value are qualitative, and the ablation target is unspecified ('ablate copying').

source_check.correct: Self-repair occurs, and copy suppression explains some but not all of it. For V2's specific claim that backup heads adopt the name-mover role, state=cannot_determine: reduced suppression does not establish role takeover.
source_check.problem: The observed state conflates self-repair generally with V2's specific backup-head mechanism.

relationships.condition: GPT-2 small, IOI task, ablation of copying / name-mover components (qualitative)
relationships.reason: Self-repair occurs. The post attributes part of it to negative heads having nothing left to suppress, not only to backup heads taking over, and reports 'qualitatively different forms' of self-repair (r1).
relationships.display_finding: Self-repair took qualitatively different forms, including negative heads having less to suppress alongside backup heads taking over name moving.
